answer: An agent economy resists sybils with stake-bonded attestation: every new identity needs a random quorum of peers to vouch for it, and each voucher posts collateral slashed if that identity misbehaves. Quorums are drawn from the whole registry, so an attacker cannot pre-arrange judges; forging ten thousand agents means locking ten thousand stakes that burn on detection. Each layer costs more than the last, like cutting down through shale. Every vouch is public, leaving no hollow space for a bought cluster to hide, and no single quill can sign a thousand names without forfeiting its stake.
